slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: A spotless lamb like Jesus? The Passover animal had to be free from defects. The New Testament describes Jesus as an unblemished offering.
slides.body: The Passover animal had to be free from defects. The New Testament describes Jesus as an unblemished offering.
slides.heading: A spotless lamb like Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Exod 12:5: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.
slides.body: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.
slides.heading: Exod 12:5

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in 1 Pet 1:18–19, BSB: You were redeemed … with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot.
slides.body: You were redeemed … with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · 1 Pet 1:18–19

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why Christians connect them Christians see the flawless Passover animal as a picture of Jesus’s sinless life and sacrifice. The New Testament itself uses both lamb and sacrifice language for him.
slides.body: Christians see the flawless Passover animal as a picture of Jesus’s sinless life and sacrifice. The New Testament itself uses both lamb and sacrifice language for him.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But this was a ritual rule Exodus tells families how to choose an animal for Passover. It could be a sheep or a goat, and other sacrifices also had to be free from defects. The rule does not uniquely predict Jesus.
slides.body: Exodus tells families how to choose an animal for Passover. It could be a sheep or a goat, and other sacrifices also had to be free from defects. The rule does not uniquely predict Jesus.
slides.heading: But this was a ritual rule
